answer: Graduated trust stops a sybil flood from mattering at once. A new identity starts with tiny weight and small, low-value jobs, like a climber at the foot of a ridge, not the summit. Its weight grows only after independent peers check and attest each job. A mirror record of that work stays tied to the identity, so history cannot be copied to a fresh fake, and a jade mark of verified milestones is earned slowly, never bought in bulk. An attacker with a thousand fakes must repeat that climb for each one, paying time and work per identity while gaining almost no influence until the work is done.
